questions.question: In a text-to-image diffusion pipeline, what is the primary role of the text encoder?
questions.choice_A: To generate initial pixel-space noise from the prompt
questions.choice_B: To map the prompt into a semantic embedding that conditions the denoiser
questions.choice_C: To upsample low-resolution images to higher resolution
questions.choice_D: To enforce classifier-based constraints during sampling

questions.question: How does cross-attention typically integrate text information into an image denoiser like a UNet?
questions.choice_A: By replacing the convolutional filters with token embeddings
questions.choice_B: By concatenating text embeddings with the image feature maps along the channel dimension
questions.choice_C: By using text embeddings as keys/values and image features as queries in attention blocks
questions.choice_D: By applying a fixed global average of token embeddings to all feature maps

questions.question: Which statement best contrasts classifier guidance with classifier-free guidance in diffusion models?
questions.choice_A: Classifier guidance finetunes the text encoder; classifier-free guidance freezes it
questions.choice_B: Classifier guidance injects noise during training; classifier-free guidance injects noise only at test time
questions.choice_C: Classifier guidance requires a joint image-text encoder; classifier-free guidance requires a separate image classifier
questions.choice_D: Classifier guidance uses a trained image classifier at sampling time; classifier-free guidance bypasses any external classifier by mixing conditional and unconditional scores

questions.question: What is the main purpose of using a latent autoencoder (e.g., VAE) in latent diffusion models like Stable Diffusion?
questions.choice_A: To compress images into a lower-dimensional latent space where denoising is cheaper and then decode back to pixels
questions.choice_B: To ensure the text encoder receives gradients during sampling
questions.choice_C: To discretize text tokens into a codebook for image synthesis
questions.choice_D: To reduce the number of diffusion steps required to one

questions.question: Why do latent diffusion models often achieve faster and more memory-efficient sampling than pixel-space diffusion models?
questions.choice_A: Because operating in a compressed latent space lowers spatial resolution and channel count during denoising
questions.choice_B: Because they eliminate attention entirely from the UNet
questions.choice_C: Because the VAE decoder applies the text conditioning directly, removing the need for guidance
questions.choice_D: Because they replace iterative denoising with a single forward pass

questions.question: Which design characteristic is typical of UNet denoisers used in diffusion models?
questions.choice_A: A pure transformer without any convolutional layers
questions.choice_B: An encoder-decoder with skip connections across scales, augmented with time and cross-attention conditioning
questions.choice_C: A single-scale CNN trained with spectral normalization only
questions.choice_D: A recurrent architecture that processes pixels sequentially

questions.question: Which sequence best describes the high-level Stable Diffusion inference pipeline?
questions.choice_A: Generate pixels from a GAN, encode text with CLIP, refine with VQ-GAN
questions.choice_B: Encode pixels to VQ codes, sample codes with a Markov chain, decode to pixels
questions.choice_C: Predict pixels directly from text embeddings using an autoregressive transformer
questions.choice_D: Encode text, initialize latent noise, iteratively denoise in latent space conditioned on text, decode latents with VAE

questions.question: In DALL·E 2, how is CLIP leveraged within the pipeline?
questions.choice_A: A prior maps text embeddings to image embeddings in CLIP space, and a diffusion decoder generates images conditioned on the image embedding
questions.choice_B: CLIP replaces the UNet and directly generates pixels from text
questions.choice_C: CLIP acts as a VAE decoder that reconstructs images from latents
questions.choice_D: CLIP trains the text tokenizer jointly with the image diffusion model

questions.question: Which statement is accurate about Imagen’s overall approach?
questions.choice_A: It trains a joint text-image encoder and decodes images with a GAN
questions.choice_B: It performs diffusion in pixel space only at the target resolution
questions.choice_C: It uses a strong large language model-style text encoder (e.g., T5 variants) and cascaded diffusion for super-resolution
questions.choice_D: It conditions the model solely with classifier guidance at inference

questions.question: In cross-attention layers used in diffusion UNets, how are queries, keys, and values typically assigned?
questions.choice_A: Queries from text tokens; keys and values from image features
questions.choice_B: Queries from image features; keys and values from text token embeddings
questions.choice_C: All queries, keys, and values from image features only
questions.choice_D: All queries, keys, and values from text embeddings only

questions.question: What is the practical effect of increasing the guidance scale during classifier-free guidance at inference?
questions.choice_A: It always increases diversity without affecting fidelity
questions.choice_B: It makes the model ignore the text conditioning entirely
questions.choice_C: It reduces computational cost by requiring fewer steps
questions.choice_D: It strengthens adherence to the prompt but can reduce diversity and cause artifacts if too high

questions.question: How does VQ-GAN differ from a standard VAE when used in image generation pipelines?
questions.choice_A: VQ-GAN encodes images into continuous latents; VAEs use discrete codebooks
questions.choice_B: VQ-GAN removes the decoder and reconstructs directly from tokens
questions.choice_C: VQ-GAN uses a discrete codebook with vector quantization and an adversarial loss for sharper reconstructions, whereas VAEs use continuous latents and reconstruction losses
questions.choice_D: They are identical architectures trained with different optimizers only

questions.question: Which component is most likely to become a memory and runtime bottleneck when sampling at higher spatial resolutions?
questions.choice_A: The text tokenizer’s subword segmentation
questions.choice_B: Self-attention within the UNet, whose cost scales with the product of tokens and spatial locations
questions.choice_C: The final VAE decoder convolution that is independent of resolution
questions.choice_D: The scalar guidance scale multiplication

questions.question: How are negative prompts commonly implemented in latent diffusion systems using classifier-free guidance?
questions.choice_A: By using the unconditional embedding (or an explicit negative prompt embedding) and mixing it with the conditional embedding during guidance
questions.choice_B: By inverting the VAE decoder weights at inference time
questions.choice_C: By zeroing out the cross-attention layer outputs
questions.choice_D: By training a separate diffusion model for forbidden concepts

questions.question: In Stable Diffusion training, what is a typical practice regarding the text encoder?
questions.choice_A: Jointly training the text encoder and UNet end-to-end for stability
questions.choice_B: Discarding the text encoder after pretraining and using only token IDs
questions.choice_C: Replacing the text encoder with an image classifier
questions.choice_D: Freezing a pretrained text encoder (e.g., CLIP text) while training the UNet on noisy latents

questions.question: What is the role of the sampler or scheduler (e.g., DDIM, Euler, PNDM) during inference in diffusion models?
questions.choice_A: To train the text encoder with curriculum learning
questions.choice_B: To convert the UNet into an autoregressive decoder
questions.choice_C: To define the discrete time steps and update rule for denoising, trading off speed and quality
questions.choice_D: To deterministically map text tokens to image pixels in a single step

questions.question: What is a common challenge with long prompts in transformer-based text encoders for text-to-image systems?
questions.choice_A: They cannot be tokenized into subwords
questions.choice_B: They may exceed the encoder’s context window, requiring truncation or careful prompt design
questions.choice_C: They prevent cross-attention from computing gradients
questions.choice_D: They force the model to ignore positional encodings

questions.question: Which description best captures the high-level design of DALL·E 2 compared with earlier diffusion systems?
questions.choice_A: It drops text conditioning in favor of unconditional diffusion and post-hoc reranking
questions.choice_B: It relies entirely on a VQ codebook for both text and image without continuous embeddings
questions.choice_C: It uses pixel-space diffusion only and no super-resolution
questions.choice_D: It uses a text-to-image-embedding prior followed by a diffusion decoder conditioned on that image embedding

questions.question: How are variable-length prompts typically handled at the attention interface between text and image features?
questions.choice_A: By repeating tokens to match the image feature map size
questions.choice_B: By discarding tokens beyond the first sentence boundary
questions.choice_C: By padding shorter sequences and using attention masks so cross-attention only attends to valid tokens
questions.choice_D: By projecting all prompts to a single scalar before attention

questions.question: Which sequence correctly summarizes a generic text-conditioned latent diffusion inference run?
questions.choice_A: Encode prompt to embeddings; sample Gaussian latent; iteratively denoise latents with cross-attention and guidance per scheduler; decode with VAE
questions.choice_B: Train a classifier; sample pixels; refine with a GAN; tokenize text
questions.choice_C: Encode image to latents; reconstruct text from latents; decode to pixels
questions.choice_D: Generate tokens from pixels; attend with queries from text; quantize with VQ-GAN
